about.text: Cheese eaten young, with little or no ripening, so it stays soft, moist and mild and keeps only briefly: under German cheese law it holds more than 73 % water in the cheese without its fat. Set with rennet, as these are, or mainly with acid, as quark and cottage cheese are.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Fresh cheese is drained and eaten straight away, without ripening, so it stays moist (more than 73 % water in the fat-free mass under German law) and mild.

steps.note: Mostly acid-set, with a little rennet.

processing.text: Only the lactic kind is soured; the rennet-set kind (queso fresco, Mató, Stracchino) is not. No ripening.
